claims.statement: DECISION-CRITICAL / market stock: URE counted 1,636,673 renewable micro-installations at year-end 2025, of which 99.9% were PV and 1,612,450 were prosumer installations.
DECISION-CRITICAL / pain: almost one-third of the URE coordinator's 2025 electricity applications came from prosumers, with recurring voltage shutdown, billing, meter, and configuration issues.

DECISION-CRITICAL / incidence boundary: the URE coordinator received 318 qualifying matters across energy markets, including 267 electricity matters, so this self-selected dispute set cannot estimate problem incidence or economic loss across 1.6 million installations.

DECISION-CRITICAL / Polish spend benchmark: Pionier listed PV care at 29 or 119 PLN gross per month for consumers, 399 PLN net per month for a business installation up to 50 kW, and 1,199 PLN gross for an on-site fault diagnosis.

DECISION-CRITICAL / observed buyer behaviour: Otovo Poland lists 39, 109, and 199 PLN monthly memberships and states that about 80% of members select the 109 PLN Prime plan; this is first-party behavioural evidence without a disclosed Polish denominator, cohort, churn, or audit.

DECISION-CRITICAL / workaround: Otovo's Polish offer bundles proactive monitoring, phone troubleshooting, warranty administration, repair coordination, discounts, and response guarantees, and states that eight of ten faults are resolved remotely; buyers are purchasing a service outcome rather than telemetry alone.

DECISION-CRITICAL / realised revenue: Otovo reported NOK 5.576 million of recurring-services revenue and NOK 31.093 million of field-services revenue in Q2 2026, confirming actual spend on service models while mixing geographies and multiple recurring products.

DECISION-CRITICAL / unit economics: Otovo's reported segment figures imply about 94% gross profit for recurring services and about 18% for field services, but recurring-services gross profit excludes unallocated payroll and operating expense and the group still reported a NOK 70 million operating loss in Q2 2026.

DECISION-CRITICAL / operational density: Otovo explicitly said field-service margins were affected by technician training, integration, and supply-chain growth and that some geographies need more density before underlying margins are realised.

DECISION-CRITICAL / acquisition route: Otovo obtained exclusive marketing access to an installer portfolio and assumed warranties on 417 commercial installations for shares valued at USD 425,000 plus a variable annual fee, demonstrating that a portfolio partnership may carry material acquisition consideration.

DECISION-CRITICAL / API cost: SolarEdge lists USD 100, 400, and 1,000 monthly developer tiers for 20,000, 100,000, and 400,000 credits and says charges begin 1 November 2026; at only 100 sites, the smallest paid tier alone is USD 1 per site per month before hosting, support, other vendors, and credit sufficiency.

DECISION-CRITICAL / integration durability: SolarEdge says its legacy Monitoring API will be deprecated on 1 November 2026 as its new paid platform takes over, illustrating vendor-change and migration cost.

DECISION-CRITICAL / incumbent response: SolarEdge markets lifetime-free monitoring and automatic production-problem alerts to system owners, so generic monitoring and alerting are already bundled with hardware for SolarEdge sites.

DECISION-CRITICAL / multi-vendor cost: Fronius offers an O&M-capable production API only after registration and contract, with automatic monthly billing by data package; five-minute historical data can create a billable point for every channel and timestamp.

DECISION-CRITICAL / competitive overlap: SOLARMAN Business already advertises consolidated fleet visibility, third-party inverter support, alerts with causes and maintenance suggestions, smart O&M, and AI analysis.
DECISION-CRITICAL / data access: the EU Data Act applies from 12 September 2025 and enables users to share readily available raw and pre-processed connected-product data with a chosen third party.

DECISION-CRITICAL / data-access limits: inferred and derived data are outside Data Act scope; data holders can seek reasonable compensation and apply trade-secret or security safeguards, while personal data still need a valid legal basis.

DECISION-CRITICAL / regulation and operations: the European Commission says smart-meter and energy-use data affect privacy and personal-data protection and highlights growing energy-sector cybersecurity risk; authorisation alone does not remove GDPR and security duties.

DECISION-CRITICAL / buyer-list scope: UDT says its free register contains more than 9,500 certified installers across Poland, but the described fields identify individuals and certificates rather than firms, fleet sizes, support obligations, budgets, or buying authority.

DECISION-CRITICAL / pain is not WTP: prosumer disputes prove recurring pain types, and paid care offers prove some consumer demand for bundled outcomes, but no source shows that Polish installers will pay recurring per-site fees for standalone triage software.

DECISION-CRITICAL / partner category is not channel: the UDT list can seed outreach and OEM or distributor relationships may create introductions, but only signed referral or portfolio-access terms plus measured paid conversion establish a channel; Otovo's paid access transaction is contrary evidence to assuming it is free.

DECISION-CRITICAL / buyer list is not affordable access: 9,500 certified individuals do not reveal which entities retain support portfolios or how many founder hours and paid touches are required to reach a decision-maker; no current source establishes Polish installer CAC.

DECISION-CRITICAL / data is not moat: legal access rights, commercial OEM APIs, free OEM monitoring, and an existing multi-vendor AI O&M product make raw telemetry and generic anomaly detection replicable; only exclusive labelled resolutions and embedded workflows could compound.

DECISION-CRITICAL / avoided loss is not capturable revenue: the homeowner bears lost generation and a grid-voltage problem may require DSO action, while an installer may bill a field diagnosis; only unreimbursed warranty, labour, and travel cost demonstrably removed by the tool belongs in installer ROI.

DECISION-CRITICAL / conservative pricing: because Polish retail plans bundle human service at 29-199 PLN monthly and OEM monitoring is free, a wholesale software test should start around 3-6 PLN per connected site with a 500 PLN minimum, not assume the original 8-15 PLN range; this remains an unvalidated hypothesis.

DECISION-CRITICAL / conservative margin: a read-only product should underwrite only 60-75% fully loaded gross margin after API, hosting, onboarding, and review; managed field work should remain outside SaaS revenue because a scaled incumbent reported about 18% field-service segment gross profit before corporate overhead.

DECISION-CRITICAL / founder outcome path: at 5 PLN per site per month, 15% EBITDA, a 3x EBITDA value, and 70% founder ownership, about 265,000 paying sites are required for 5 million PLN of founder equity value, roughly 16% of Poland's 2025 prosumer stock; no evidenced channel supports this penetration.

DECISION-CRITICAL / founder feasibility: a manual, read-only, one-portfolio pilot is compatible with the founder's skills, family-company access, time ceiling, and initial capital, but a national multi-vendor monitoring, dispatch, and support operation is not feasible part-time without hired operations and substantially more capital.

DECISION-CRITICAL / minimum viable test: the next product should be a paid 90-day concierge exception desk for one or two vendors, with remote control and dispatch excluded, and should advance only if independent installers renew after measured net savings exceed fees.
DECISION-CRITICAL / unresolved demand: independent Polish installer paid-pilot conversion, renewal, site retention, and fully loaded CAC remain unknown.

DECISION-CRITICAL / unresolved technical economics: brand-weighted API coverage, data quality, polling requirements, false-alert rates, and fully loaded cost at 100, 1,000, and 10,000 connected sites remain unknown.

contrary_evidence: Generic monitoring is already lifetime-free for SolarEdge owners and available inside other OEM portals.
SOLARMAN Business already markets multi-device and third-party-inverter visibility, diagnoses, maintenance suggestions, and AI-assisted O&M.
Otovo Poland already bundles monitoring, remote troubleshooting, warranty handling, dispatch coordination, and repair discounts at 39-199 PLN per month.

Otovo's Q2 2026 filing shows a scaled incumbent using acquisitions and paid portfolio-access agreements; its group still lost NOK 70 million in the quarter despite high reported recurring-service segment gross profit.
Otovo's field-services segment produced only about 18% gross profit before unallocated corporate costs, directly contradicting software-like assumptions for managed dispatch and repair.
The URE complaint evidence is a small, self-selected dispute population and does not establish prevalence, support cost, or installer purchasing intent.
Polish service price lists demonstrate bundled care offers, not paid adoption of a standalone B2B software layer.
SolarEdge is moving to a paid API with fixed monthly tiers, and Fronius requires a contract and usage-based data package, so integration cost can consume a low per-site fee at small scale.
The EU Data Act supports access to some user-generated raw data but excludes inferred or derived data and preserves compensation, trade-secret, security, and GDPR constraints.
A public register of certified installers does not identify portfolio owners or demonstrate affordable decision-maker access.

unknowns: Count of actively supported sites per target firm, segmented by vendor, system age, warranty status, and accessible credentials.
Baseline tickets per 100 sites per month and the mix of remotely resolvable, DSO, billing, warranty, and physical faults.
Fully loaded staff cost, unreimbursed travel cost, warranty cost, customer churn cost, and revenue lost when visits are avoided.
Paid-pilot conversion among at least three non-family installers and the objections of firms that decline.
Whether the payer is the installer, an O&M firm, or a homeowner care-plan subscriber; the evidence does not resolve this.
Exact SolarEdge credit consumption and Fronius data-point consumption for useful anomaly latency and breadth.
Commercial API access, owner-consent mechanics, and reliable alert coverage for the other inverter brands in the family company's installed base.
Accuracy and incremental decision value of the proposed evidence packs compared with staff using existing portals and templates.
Legal roles, data minimisation design, DPIA need, insurance availability, incident-response cost, and contractual liability allocation.
Cash CAC, founder-hour CAC, sales-cycle duration, and portfolio migration cost outside the family-company route.
Renewal, connected-site churn, expansion revenue, and support load after the first 90 days.
Whether labelled outcome data can be made contractually reusable and sufficiently exclusive to create any compounding advantage.
Whether an OEM, SOLARMAN, or Otovo can replicate the evidence-pack workflow before the entrant reaches scale.
A financially credible route to the founder's wealth objective without acquiring an implausibly large share of Poland's prosumer fleet or adding low-margin field operations.
